ic_name: ARM CoreSight On-Chip Debug and Trace Architecture

frs_sections.title: SCOPE AND PURPOSE
frs_sections.content:
CoreSight is ARM's on-chip debug and trace framework. It is the architecture
that ties together the debug access path, the trace generation sources, the
trace transport, the trace capture sinks, and the cross-trigger fabric of a
System-on-Chip. CoreSight is NOT itself a wire-level transport such as JTAG or
Serial Wire Debug (SWD); rather it is the architecture that SITS ON TOP of a
JTAG or SWD transport and turns a chip into a debuggable, traceable system.
A CoreSight system is discoverable: an external debugger walks a hierarchy of
ROM Tables and reads each component's identification registers to enumerate the
debug and trace components present on the device.

A complete CoreSight subsystem is built from the following classes of block:

frs_sections.title: TRACE SOURCES
frs_sections.content:
A trace source generates a trace stream and emits it onto the AMBA Trace Bus.
The architected CoreSight trace sources are:

3.1 ETM (Embedded Trace Macrocell), including ETMv4 (the ETMv4 architecture is
also called the ETM architecture used by modern cores). An ETM observes a
processor and produces instruction trace (program flow: branches taken, the
addresses of indirect branches and exceptions) and optionally data trace
(addresses and/or values of load/store accesses). ETM trace is highly
compressed: the decoder reconstructs full program flow from a small number of
trace bytes plus the program image. An ETM is configured through its CoreSight
debug registers (trace enable, address-range comparators, context-ID
comparators, counters, sequencer, and the ATB trace ID register TRCTRACEIDR).
…

frs_sections.title: TRACE SINKS
frs_sections.content:
A trace sink terminates a trace stream. The architected CoreSight trace sinks
are:

5.1 TPIU (Trace Port Interface Unit). The TPIU formats the on-chip ATB trace and
drives it off-chip on a parallel trace port (the Trace Port: a trace clock
TRACECLK plus trace data lines TRACEDATA[n], typically 1/2/4/8/16 data lines)
or, on a Serial Wire system, onto the Serial Wire Output (SWO) single pin. The
TPIU applies the trace-port framing/formatter so the external Trace Port
Analyzer can recover the interleaved trace and split it by trace ID.

5.2 ETB (Embedded Trace Buffer). An on-chip circular RAM that captures the ATB
trace stream when no off-chip trace port is available or affordable. The
debugger drains the ETB over the Debug APB after the capture window.

frs_sections.title: CLAIM, LOCK, AND POWER/STATUS MANAGEMENT REGISTERS
frs_sections.content:
In addition to the identification registers, CoreSight components share a set of
management registers near the top of their register block:
  - CLAIMSET / CLAIMCLR: claim-tag bits that let multiple debug agents (an
    external debugger and on-target self-hosted debug) cooperate without
    clobbering each other.
  - LAR (Lock Access Register) / LSR (Lock Status Register): a software lock that
    must be unlocked (by writing the lock key) before the component's registers
    can be modified from memory-mapped accesses.
  - AUTHSTATUS: reports the current debug authentication permissions for the
    component (see section 9).
  - DEVID / DEVAFF: device configuration and affinity (which processor a
    component is associated with).

frs_sections.title: DEBUG AUTHENTICATION
frs_sections.content:
Invasive and non-invasive debug, at both the Non-secure and Secure security
states, are individually gated by authentication signals presented to each
debug/trace component:
  - DBGEN: invasive debug enable (Non-secure). Allows halting-mode debug.
  - NIDEN: non-invasive debug enable (Non-secure). Allows trace and the PMU.
  - SPIDEN: Secure invasive debug enable. Allows invasive debug of Secure state.
  - SPNIDEN: Secure non-invasive debug enable. Allows trace of Secure state.
The AUTHSTATUS register of each component reflects which of these are currently
permitted. A production device typically deasserts the Secure (and possibly all)
authentication signals so that an attacker cannot use the debug architecture to
read Secure assets; a development device asserts them. These signals are the…

frs_sections.title: RELATIONSHIP TO, AND DISTINCTION FROM, JTAG AND SWD
frs_sections.content:
CoreSight is deliberately layered above the JTAG and SWD transports and must not
be confused with them:
  - JTAG (IEEE 1149.1) is a boundary-scan / test-access transport: a TAP state
    machine driven by TCK/TMS/TDI/TDO with an instruction register and data
    registers. A pure JTAG document with only the TAP state machine, boundary
    scan, BYPASS/IDCODE/EXTEST instructions, and no DAP/AP, no ATB, no funnel,
    no trace source/sink, and no ROM-table discovery is NOT a CoreSight document.
  - SWD (Serial Wire Debug) is the two-wire ADIv5 Debug Port transport (SWDIO,
    SWCLK) with packet request / ACK / data phases and the DP CTRL/STAT and
    SELECT registers. A pure SWD/ADIv5 Debug-Port document with only the
    serial-wire line protocol and DP registers, and no Access Ports onto a…

frs_sections.title: VERSIONING NOTE
frs_sections.content:
CoreSight has evolved across architecture generations (commonly referred to as
CoreSight v1/v2/v3 in public material). Later generations add the DEVARCH
register (architecture identification), refine the component identification
scheme, and extend the trace and cross-trigger components (for example ETMv4 and
the CoreSight Trace Memory Controller realizing ETF/ETR). The DAP itself follows
the ARM Debug Interface versions ADIv5 and ADIv6. Exact register bit layouts,
the number of stimulus ports on an STM, the depth of an ETB/ETF, the number of
TPIU trace-data pins, and the number of CTM channels are all
implementation-defined and are not fixed by this overview.

protocol_overview.type: On-chip debug and trace ARCHITECTURE layered over a JTAG (IEEE 1149.1 TAP) or SWD (Serial Wire Debug / ADIv5) transport. Comprises a Debug Access Port (DAP = Debug Port + Access Ports onto the on-chip debug bus), trace sources (ETM/PTM/ITM/STM), an ATB trace transport with funnels and replicators, trace sinks (TPIU/ETB/ETF/ETR), and a CTI/CTM cross-trigger fabric.
wire_names_optional: nTRST (only in SWJ-DP variants exposing TRST)
protocol_overview.controller_role: Debug host (USB-to-SWD probe such as J-Link / ST-Link / CMSIS-DAP) drives SWCLK out and bidirectionally drives or tri-states SWDIO; sequences 46-bit transactions; sets SELECT for AP+bank addressing; reads RDBUFF to recover the final posted read.
protocol_overview.target_role: Target SoC implements SW-DP (or SWJ-DP) at the wire layer + DP register set + one or more APs (MEM-AP, JTAG-AP, etc.); decodes 8-bit Request, drives the 3-bit ACK, and either drives the 33-bit read data + parity (for reads) or samples the 33-bit write data + parity (for writes).

layered_on_transport.jtag: JTAG-DP: IEEE 1149.1 TAP (TCK/TMS/TDI/TDO) reaches the DAP.
layered_on_transport.swd: SW-DP: Serial Wire (SWDIO/SWCLK), ADIv5 Debug Port.
layered_on_transport.swj: SWJ-DP: pins switchable between SWD and JTAG.
layered_on_transport.note: CoreSight is NOT the transport; it is the architecture on top of the transport.

debug_access_port.note: The DP terminates the transport and performs the debug/system power-up handshake; the AP masters an on-chip bus for memory-mapped register/memory access.

trace_transport.trace_id: each source carries an ATB trace ID (TRACEIDR/TRCTRACEIDR) so the merged stream can be demultiplexed
trace_transport.flow_control: ATB ATVALID/ATREADY back-pressure stalls upstream sources; AFVALID/AFREADY flush signaling

cross_trigger.cti: Cross Trigger Interface per component — maps local trigger in/out onto channels
cross_trigger.ctm: Cross Trigger Matrix — broadcasts channel events between CTIs
cross_trigger.use: synchronous multi-core halt/restart, ETM trigger, PMU events

discovery.rom_table: MEM-AP BASE points at the top-level ROM Table; the table tree lists component offsets

compliance_requirements: A DAP with a conformant Debug Port (ADIv5/ADIv6) and at least one Access Port reaching the debug register space.
Debug registers memory-mapped (Debug APB), 4 KB per component, with standard CIDR/PIDR/DEVARCH/DEVTYPE identification registers.
At least one trace source (ETM/ITM/STM) emitting onto the ATB with a trace ID, and a trace sink (TPIU/ETB/ETF/ETR) to capture it; funnel/replicator where multiple streams/sinks are present.
A discoverable ROM-Table hierarchy from the MEM-AP BASE register.
Debug authentication gating (DBGEN/NIDEN/SPIDEN/SPNIDEN) and AUTHSTATUS reporting.
Cross-trigger (CTI/CTM) where multi-component event distribution is required.

functional_requirements.text: An external debugger SHALL access the on-chip debug bus through a Debug Access Port (DAP): a Debug Port (SW-DP / JTAG-DP / SWJ-DP) terminating the JTAG/SWD transport plus one or more Access Ports (AHB-AP / APB-AP / AXI-AP / JTAG-AP).

The Debug Port SHALL own the DP registers (DPIDR/IDCODE, CTRL/STAT, SELECT, RDBUFF) and SHALL perform the debug and system power-up handshake (CDBGPWRUPREQ/ACK, CSYSPWRUPREQ/ACK) before accesses proceed.
Each MEM-AP SHALL expose CSW, TAR, DRW, BD0-BD3, CFG, BASE, and IDR; the debugger reaches a component by programming TAR with its base address and transferring through DRW.
CoreSight debug registers SHALL be memory-mapped (over a Debug APB), with each component occupying a 4 KB register block.
Trace sources (ETM/ETMv4, PTM, ITM, STM) SHALL generate trace and emit it onto the ATB, each tagging its stream with an ATB trace ID.
Trace SHALL be carried on the AMBA Trace Bus (ATB); funnels SHALL combine multiple ATB input streams into one and replicators SHALL fan one ATB stream out to multiple outputs.
Trace sinks SHALL terminate the stream: the TPIU drives it off-chip (trace port / SWO); the ETB and ETF capture it in on-chip RAM; the ETR routes it into system memory over AXI.
A Cross Trigger Interface (CTI) per component, linked by the Cross Trigger Matrix (CTM), SHALL distribute debug events (e.g. halt/restart) across components.

The system SHALL be discoverable: the MEM-AP BASE points at a top-level ROM Table; walking the ROM Table tree and reading each component's CIDR/PIDR/DEVARCH/DEVTYPE enumerates all debug and trace components.
Invasive and non-invasive debug, Secure and Non-secure, SHALL be gated by DBGEN/NIDEN/SPIDEN/SPNIDEN; each component's AUTHSTATUS SHALL reflect the current permissions.
Components SHALL provide a software lock (LAR/LSR) and claim tags (CLAIMSET/CLAIMCLR) so multiple debug agents can coordinate without clobbering each other.

configurations.name: Pure SWD-DP target
configurations.description: The SoC implements only the 2-pin SW-DP variant — no JTAG support.

configurations.name: SWJ-DP target
configurations.description: The SoC implements the mode-switchable SWJ-DP — supports both SWD (2-pin) and JTAG (4-pin) on the same pads.

configurations.name: Multi-drop SWD
configurations.description: Two or more SWJ-DP targets share SWDIO/SWCLK on a single 2-wire connector (ADIv5.2+).

configurations.name: Single-MEM-AP DAP
configurations.description: A DAP with exactly one MEM-AP exposing a single system-bus (typical Cortex-M0/M0+ implementation).

configurations.name: Multi-AP DAP
configurations.description: A DAP with multiple APs — typical Cortex-A or multi-core SoCs.

error_response_conditions: DP CTRL/STAT sticky error flags (e.g. WDATAERR, STICKYERR, STICKYORUN) — a faulted DAP access; must be cleared before continuing.
MEM-AP access fault — addressed location not accessible (power down, permission, or no slave).
Power-up handshake not granted (CDBGPWRUPACK/CSYSPWRUPACK low) — debug logic not powered; accesses cannot proceed.
Authentication denied (DBGEN/NIDEN/SPIDEN/SPNIDEN deasserted) — invasive or Secure debug refused; AUTHSTATUS shows it.
ATB back-pressure / overflow — a sink cannot accept trace fast enough; the funnel/source stalls or trace is dropped (sink-dependent).
Locked component (LSR shows locked) — register writes ignored until the lock key is written to LAR.
